# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**Emerson Jennings**
Member ID: W359699103
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Iowa Total Care — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-09 — Reference number POC-3A565C0679-61883**
**Member:** Emerson Jennings | **Member ID:** W359699103
**Service denied:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar fusion (CPT 22612) that my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, requested on my behalf. The notice dated 2026-08-09 states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery.

I am asking Iowa Total Care to reconsider that decision. My records document a supervised, multimodal course of conservative care that did not relieve my symptoms, and they document imaging findings that match my clinical exam. Below, I quote the plan's own criteria from the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines and show where each one is met in my records.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The plan's conservative-care requirement**

The 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines state:

> "Failure of conservative treatment\* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months"

My records establish this. I completed supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-10 — 10 weeks, with 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That course ran in the months immediately before the surgery was requested. In addition, I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.

**2. How the plan defines "failure"**

The Guidelines state:

> "NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: ■ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR ■ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR ■ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment"

Only one of those three needs to be met. My records meet the first: I finished a full course of physical therapy — all 20 visits — and I did not get meaningful improvement. My symptoms have been progressive over 24 months of pain in my lower back and legs, unrelieved by rest. I still cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, and I get relief only by sitting.

I would also point out the related note in the Guidelines:

> "Closure of medical or therapy offices, patient inconvenience, or noncompliance without explanation does not constitute “inability to complete” treatment."

That provision does not apply to me. I did not fail to complete treatment. I attended and finished the full course, and the conservative care failed on its own terms.

**3. The plan's multimodality requirement**

The Guidelines state:

> "Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region."

My care included both an active and an inactive component, and both targeted my lumbar spine. The active component was supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. The inactive components were NSAIDs over 6 months and the lumbar corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21.

**4. Imaging that matches the clinical findings**

The Guidelines require:

> "Imaging studies corresponding to the clinical findings"

My imaging on 2026-07-08 — MRI of the lumbar spine plus flexion-extension radiographs — showed grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. My exam findings are neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, with no bowel or bladder dysfunction. The imaging and the exam point to the same level and the same problem.

**5. The listed clinical conditions**

The Guidelines list, among the qualifying conditions:

> "Spondylolisthesis (neural arch defect - spondylolytic spondylolisthesis, degenerative spondylolisthesis, and congenital unilateral neural arch hypoplasia)"

and

> "Evidence of segmental instability - Excessive motion, as in degenerative spondylolisthesis, segmental instability, and surgically induced segmental instability"

My imaging documents degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 — named in both provisions — together with 5 mm of translation measured on flexion-extension films, which is motion documented on dynamic imaging.

**6. Symptom duration**

The Guidelines describe:

> "Lumbar back pain, neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain without sensory or motor deficit that impairs daily activities for at least 6 months"

My symptoms have lasted 24 months, well beyond six months, and they impair my daily activities — I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes. In the interest of accuracy, I note that my exam also records diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes.

**7. A clear surgical plan**

The Guidelines state:

> "In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery."

Dr. Reyes has documented the need for this procedure, and the surgical plan in my chart is the lumbar fusion submitted under CPT 22612.

**Provisions I am not relying on.** For completeness: my records do not describe a prior lumbar operation, a spinal tumor, cancer, or infection, and I have no bowel or bladder dysfunction. So the Guidelines' provisions on revision surgery for pseudoarthrosis or repeat disk herniation, fusion for tumor/cancer/infection, and cauda equina syndrome are not the basis of my appeal. I also note that the excerpt of the Guidelines available to me introduces lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material I have, so there may be additional criteria I have not been able to address.

## Please send me the criteria that were actually applied

The denial notice says the decision was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not identify which criterion my records were found not to meet. The plan holds those criteria; I do not. I am asking Iowa Total Care to provide me, in writing and free of charge, the specific clinical review criteria applied to this request, the name and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination, and confirmation of whether this request was reviewed by Evolent under the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines. If a specific number of weeks, visits, or months was used as the threshold here, please state it and identify where it appears in the policy, so that I can respond to it directly.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask that Iowa Total Care overturn the denial dated 2026-08-09 (reference POC-3A565C0679-61883) and authorize the lumbar fusion, CPT 22612, as requested by Dr. Reyes. I also ask that the review be performed by a physician in orthopedic surgery or spine surgery, and that I receive a written decision explaining the outcome.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file using my state's appeal or grievance form at ambetterhealth.com (selecting Iowa), or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please let me know if any additional records would help. I will provide them promptly. My physical therapy discharge note, imaging reports from 2026-07-08, and Dr. Reyes's office notes are available on request.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Jennings**
Member ID: W359699103
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [List what you are sending — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-09; physical therapy discharge note; MRI and flexion-extension radiograph reports dated 2026-07-08; office notes from Dr. Reyes]

Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months

NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: ■ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR ■ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR ■ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment
Non-operative conservative treatment should include a multimodality approach consisting of at least one (1) active and one (1) inactive component targeting the affected spinal region.
Revision surgery for failed previous operation(s) for pseudoarthrosis at the same level at least 9-12 months from prior surgery if significant functional gains are anticipated
Revision surgery for failed previous operation(s) repeat disk herniations if significant functional gains are anticipated

Chronic low back pain or degenerative disc disease (disc degeneration without significant neurological compression presenting with low back pain) must have failed at least 6 months of appropriate active non-operative treatment (completion of a comprehensive cognitive-behavioral rehabilitation program is mandatory) and must be evaluated on a case-by-case basis

Progressive nerve compression resulting in an acute neurologic deficit (motor) AND ○ One of the aforementioned clinical conditions, except chronic low back pain or degenerative disc disease. The neurological deficits must be significant: 0-2/5 on the motor function scale for L5 or S1 roots OR 0-3/5 for L3 or L4 roots.
